steps.title: Start with two groups
steps.text: Our example joins 8 counters and 5 counters. How many more does 8 need to make ten?

visual.caption: Eight counters and five counters.

steps.title: Make a ten
steps.text: Move 2 from the group of 5 to the group of 8. There are 3 left. Moving counters changes the groups, not the total.

visual.caption: The same thirteen counters regrouped into ten and three.

steps.title: Join what remains
steps.text: Add the 3 remaining counters to ten. We have counted every counter once.

visual.caption: Ten and three make thirteen.

m68-02.example_prompt: There are 3 baskets with 2 apples in each. How many apples?

steps.title: Spot equal groups
steps.text: The example has 3 baskets. Each basket has 2 apples.

visual.caption: Three groups of two counters stand for the baskets.

steps.title: Count by twos
steps.text: Count one basket at a time: 2, then 4, then 6. Each jump adds two.

visual.caption: Three equal jumps of two from zero to six.

steps.title: Name the total
steps.text: Three groups of two make six apples. Multiplication is a short way to write these equal groups.

m68-03.example_prompt: Share 8 counters into 2 equal groups. How many in one half?

steps.title: Start with eight
steps.text: Share these eight counters fairly between two groups. Each group must have the same number.

visual.caption: Eight counters before sharing.

steps.title: Share equally
steps.text: Put one counter in each group, then repeat until all eight have been shared.

visual.caption: Two equal groups of four counters.

steps.title: Check one half
steps.text: One of the two equal groups has four counters. Put the two halves together to check the original eight.

visual.caption: One of two equal parts is one half.

m68-04.example_prompt: There are 12 shells. Move 3 aside. How many remain?

steps.title: Start at twelve
steps.text: There are twelve shells. We move three aside, so the number remaining gets smaller.

visual.caption: Twelve counters stand for twelve shells.

steps.title: Count back three
steps.text: Starting at 12, count back: 11, 10, 9. Count three moves, not the starting number.

visual.caption: Count backwards from twelve through eleven and ten to nine.

steps.title: Check by adding back
steps.text: Nine shells remain. The nine remaining shells and the three moved aside make twelve again.

visual.caption: Nine remaining and three moved aside still total twelve.

m68-05.example_prompt: What number is one ten and five ones?

steps.title: Find the full ten
steps.text: One ten means a group containing ten ones. Count the first group to check it.

visual.caption: One complete group of ten.

steps.title: Keep the extra ones
steps.text: There are five extra ones beside the complete ten. Keep their places separate.

visual.caption: One full ten and five extra ones.

steps.title: Read the number
steps.text: One ten and five ones make fifteen. The 1 in 15 counts tens; the 5 counts ones.

steps.title: Show one half
steps.text: Begin with one of two equal parts shaded. Keep the size of the whole unchanged.

visual.caption: One of two equal parts is shaded.

steps.title: Split every part equally
steps.text: Split both original parts into two. There are now four equal parts in the same whole; two are shaded.

visual.caption: Two of four equal parts cover the same half.

steps.title: Check the same amount
steps.text: The part size became smaller, but the shaded amount stayed the same. Multiply both numerator and denominator by the same number.

visual.caption: Two quarters are equivalent to one half.

m911-02.example_prompt: A rectangle is 6 cm long and 4 cm wide. What is its perimeter?

steps.title: Follow the outside
steps.text: Perimeter is the distance around the edge. This example rectangle has length 6 cm and width 4 cm.

visual.caption: Opposite sides match: six centimetres, four centimetres, six centimetres, four centimetres.

steps.title: Add all four sides
steps.text: Walk around once: 6, then 4, then 6, then 4. Include every side exactly once.

steps.title: Include the unit
steps.text: The total distance is twenty centimetres. We are measuring an edge, so the unit is cm.

steps.title: Name the missing part
steps.text: An unknown number plus 6 makes 15. Think of 15 as the whole and 6 as a known part.

steps.title: Undo adding six
steps.text: Subtract 6 from both sides to keep the equation balanced. The missing part is 9.

visual.caption: Nine is six less than fifteen.

steps.title: Check in the original
steps.text: Replace x with 9 and check the original addition. Both sides now have value 15.

steps.title: Use the same place value
steps.text: Write 1.2 as 1.20. The extra zero does not change its value: both mean one and twenty hundredths.

steps.title: Add equal-sized parts
steps.text: Twenty hundredths plus thirty-five hundredths make fifty-five hundredths. The one whole is still there.

steps.title: Combine and check
steps.text: One whole and fifty-five hundredths is 1.55. Adding a positive amount made the result larger than 1.20.

visual.caption: The total lies between one and two, beyond 1.20.

m911-05.example_prompt: How many minutes pass from 2:45 pm to 3:10 pm?

steps.title: Use the next hour
steps.text: Our example runs from 2:45 pm to 3:10 pm. First count from 2:45 to 3:00: fifteen minutes.

steps.title: Add the last ten minutes
steps.text: From 3:00 to 3:10 is ten more minutes. The line shows elapsed minutes, not clock readings.

visual.caption: Elapsed duration: fifteen minutes to the hour, then ten more minutes.

steps.title: Join the two durations
steps.text: Add the fifteen-minute part and the ten-minute part. Twenty-five minutes pass altogether.

m1215-01.example_prompt: A paint pattern uses red:blue beads in a 2:3 ratio. With 12 blue beads, how many red beads are needed?

steps.title: Read the relationship
steps.text: Each basic set has 2 red beads for 3 blue beads. Both colours must grow by the same factor.

visual.caption: The first group represents red and the second represents blue.

steps.title: Find the scale factor
steps.text: Blue grows from 3 to 12. Divide 12 by 3 to find a scale factor of 4.

steps.title: Scale red by the same factor
steps.text: Multiply the red count by four too. Eight red beads keep the 2:3 relationship with twelve blue beads.

visual.caption: Eight red and twelve blue preserve the original ratio.

steps.title: Choose equal-sized parts
steps.text: We need to add one quarter and one half. Rewrite the half using quarters.

visual.caption: The half is now shown as two quarters.

steps.title: Count the quarters
steps.text: Join one quarter and two quarters. The parts are still quarters; only the number of parts changes.

visual.caption: Three equal quarter-parts are shaded.

steps.title: Keep the denominator
steps.text: There are three quarters altogether. Do not add denominators: the size of each part stays one quarter.

steps.title: Undo addition first
steps.text: In 4x + 2 = 18, subtract 2 from both sides. This leaves four equal copies of x.

steps.title: Undo multiplication
steps.text: Divide both sides by 4. Four equal groups share 16, so each group has 4.

visual.caption: Sixteen counters shared into four equal groups of four.

steps.title: Substitute to check
steps.text: Put 4 back in place of x in the original equation. The left side equals the right side.

steps.title: Translate percent
steps.text: Percent means per hundred. Twenty-five per hundred is the same proportion as one quarter.

visual.caption: One quarter is twenty-five percent of the whole.

steps.title: Find a quarter of eighty
steps.text: Share eighty into four equal parts. The diagram shows the fraction of a whole, not eighty individual objects.

visual.caption: Select one of four equal shares of eighty.

steps.title: Check the amount
steps.text: Twenty is the requested percentage amount. Four groups of twenty return the original eighty.

m1215-05.example_prompt: What is the mean of 2, 4 and 9?

steps.title: Add every value
steps.text: Our three values are 2, 4 and 9. Add all three to find the total.

visual.caption: Three unequal groups contain fifteen counters in total.

steps.title: Share across three values
steps.text: There are three values, so divide the total by three. Equal sharing makes three groups of five.

visual.caption: The same fifteen counters regrouped into three equal groups of five.

steps.title: Check the mean
steps.text: The mean is 5. It need not be one of the original values. Three copies of the mean reproduce the total.
